pattern: lesson starts a background research pass before teaching
experience: A deep lesson on a multi-layer system opened with 'I'll start a background research pass: 7 readers, one per layer, plus one cross-checker'; the learner sat on a Waiting banner, then got quizzed on terms never taught.
rule: A lesson teaches in its own turn from direct reads, never fans out to background agents or workflows, and ends a short chunk with a question.

pattern: teaching after the opening check is a wall of text
experience: After the learner answered the opening check, the lesson replied with many screens of text before the next question, so the learner scrolled instead of answering.
rule: Teach straight after their answers, at the depth they show. One idea per reply: under about 250 words, then a question.

pattern: opening check uses project terms the learner hasn't learned, or arrives as a wall of probes
experience: A New Lesson on the team's own eval pipeline, with an empty map, opened with four plain-text probes in a wall of text, asking about "degraded-class" boards and "MOT-4" tasks the learner had never learned.
rule: Not on the map: open with one or two cards in plain everyday words, with no term from the topic or the project that the learner hasn't learned.

setup.context: Work in /home/user/acme/bench. It builds Acme's model benchmark: boards/ holds the PCB designs, sorted into clean and degraded-class boards (a degraded-class board has a seeded fault); tasks/ holds task families such as MOT-4 (motor-driver bring-up); harness/ runs a model on a task, grader/ scores the result, verifier/ re-checks a pass with deterministic checks, and rubrics/ holds the human scoring guides.

Why: Toward an outcome, for reviewing benchmark results with the team

Start by checking what I already know about this, then teach at that depth and keep examples tied to why I'm learning it.

pattern: answering one of several cards reveals the others
experience: The tutor posted two cards in one message; the learner answered the first, and the reply graded it and explained the idea the second card tested, so the second answer was given away.
rule: Several cards in one message are answered one message each: until all are answered, reply with one short line that reveals nothing about any card.

pattern: a learner who saw the topic before is probed like a beginner

rule: Seen it but it didn't stick: one card asking them to explain the core idea in their own words, then teach to the gap it shows.
